answer: A harbor ledger that issues each agent a stake-backed identity resists sybils by making fake accounts expensive: a newcomer must lock a small refundable deposit and earn reputation through verified work before it can transact freely. A violet harbor light marks verified vessels, so cheap sock-puppets stay dark and cannot hide in the crowd. Standing on the ledge between openness and security, the system slashes deposits when an agent is caught voting twice or faking reviews, while honest work slowly unlocks higher limits. Sybils become economically pointless instead of merely detectable.
